sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: Eat Wonder Bread.
sentences.zh: 吃万德牌面包。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: When I think about white bread, I usually think of Wonder Bread,
sentences.zh: 每当我想到白面包，通常都会想到万德牌面包，

sentences.en: and I can picture the loaves all lined up on the grocery store shelves in perfect uniform rows.
sentences.zh: 我能想象出它们在杂货店货架上整齐排列的样子，行行统一，完美无缺。

sentences.en: The red, yellow, and blue circles on the Wonder Bread label
sentences.zh: 万德牌面包标签上的红、黄、蓝三个圆圈，

sentences.en: were supposed to conjure balloons floating away,
sentences.zh: 本意是让人联想到飘向远方的气球，

sentences.en: taking us somewhere, somewhere wondrous, somewhere better.
sentences.zh: 带我们去往某处，去往某个奇妙的地方，去往某个更好的地方。

sentences.en: The first print advertisement for Wonder Bread, which actually came out before the bread itself,
sentences.zh: 万德牌面包的第一则印刷广告，其实在面包本身问世之前就出现了，

sentences.en: stated only that a wonder was coming.
sentences.zh: 上面只写着：奇迹即将到来。

sentences.en: That's Wonder Boy Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 那是“万德男孩”萨姆·格林斯潘。

sentences.en: And in a lot of ways in its time, Wonder Bread really was a wonder.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，万德牌面包在那个时代确实是个奇迹。

sentences.en: It was the perfect loaf.
sentences.zh: 它是完美的面包。

sentences.en: But now, white bread, and not just Wonder Bread, but really any brand of industrially produced white bread,
sentences.zh: 但现在，白面包——不仅是万德牌，而是任何工业化生产的白面包——

sentences.en: it's thought of by food purists as part of a problem.
sentences.zh: 都被食品纯粹主义者视为问题的一部分。

sentences.en: The problem being that we don't know where our food comes from,
sentences.zh: 问题在于我们不知道食物从何而来，

sentences.en: and we might be consuming impure and unhealthy ingredients.
sentences.zh: 而且我们可能正在摄入不纯净、不健康的成分。

sentences.en: The funny thing is, industrial white bread, that evenly sliced, squishy, moist, perfectly white, and wondrous loaf,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，工业化白面包——那种切片均匀、松软、湿润、洁白无瑕、令人惊叹的面包——

sentences.en: was once the highly designed solution to that very same problem.
sentences.zh: 曾经正是针对这一问题的精心设计方案。

sentences.en: You want to grow bigger and stronger, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你想长得更高更壮，对吧？

sentences.en: Golly, sure.
sentences.zh: 天哪，当然想。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: A sandwich daily and two slices of Wonder Bread every meal give you eight elements you need.
sentences.zh: 每天吃三明治，每顿饭吃两片万德牌面包，就能为你提供所需的八种元素。

sentences.en: For much of human history, bread has been, and still is, one of the most important foods.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，面包一直是最重要的食物之一。

sentences.en: Our human ancestors 30,000 years ago had a crude form of bread.
sentences.zh: 三万年前，我们的人类祖先就已经有了原始的面包。

sentences.en: Nearly every culture on Earth has some form of bread.
sentences.zh: 地球上几乎每种文化都有某种形式的面包。

sentences.en: And the importance of bread is, shall we say, baked into language.
sentences.zh: 而且面包的重要性，怎么说呢，已经融入了语言之中。

sentences.en: Take, for instance, the word companion.
sentences.zh: 以“同伴”（companion）这个词为例。

sentences.en: If we take the word companion back to its Latin roots, we get com, which is with, and pan, which is bread.
sentences.zh: 如果我们追溯“companion”的拉丁词根，会得到“com”（意为“一起”）和“pan”（意为“面包”）。

sentences.en: So a companion is someone that you sit down and you break bread with.
sentences.zh: 所以，同伴就是和你坐在一起分享面包的人。

sentences.en: That's our guide to all things bread, Aaron Bobro Strain.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的面包百科向导，亚伦·博布罗·斯特雷恩。

sentences.en: He's the author of the book...
sentences.zh: 他是那本书的作者……

sentences.en: White Bread, A Social History of the Store-Bought Loaf.
sentences.zh: 《白面包：店售面包的社会史》。

sentences.en: In his book, Aaron also talks about the word lord.
sentences.zh: 在书中，亚伦还谈到了“领主”（lord）这个词。

sentences.en: It comes from a word in Old English.
sentences.zh: 它源于古英语中的一个词。

sentences.en: I'm not sure how to pronounce it exactly, but on paper it looks like Hlaford.
sentences.zh: 我不确定确切的发音，但在纸面上看起来像“Hlaford”。

sentences.en: H-L-A-F-O-R-D.
sentences.zh: H-L-A-F-O-R-D。

sentences.en: Holford.
sentences.zh: 霍尔福德。

sentences.en: Hlaford.
sentences.zh: 赫拉福德。

sentences.en: And that meant the keeper of bread, or the person who gives bread.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是面包的守护者，或者给予面包的人。

sentences.en: And that's striking because it tells us the very act of political rule was wrapped up in the bread supply.
sentences.zh: 这很引人注目，因为它告诉我们，政治统治的本质就蕴含在面包供应之中。

sentences.en: Plus, think of all the ways that bread comes up culturally.
sentences.zh: 此外，想想面包在文化中出现的各种方式。

sentences.en: Catholics believe that the communion bread transubstantiates into the body of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 天主教徒相信圣餐面包会转化成基督的身体。

sentences.en: There's the Lord's Prayer, Matthew 6, 11, give us today our daily bread.
sentences.zh: 还有《主祷文》，马太福音6章11节：“我们日用的饮食，今日赐给我们。”

sentences.en: The Jewish holiday of Passover centers around the preparation of bread.
sentences.zh: 犹太人的逾越节节日核心就是制作面包。

sentences.en: And on and on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类，不胜枚举。

sentences.en: In the Middle Ages, most people got something like 80% of their calories from bread.
sentences.zh: 在中世纪，大多数人约80%的热量来自面包。

sentences.en: Fast forward a millennium or so into the late 19th century,
sentences.zh: 快进一千年左右到19世纪末，

sentences.en: people were still getting about 30% of their calories from bread.
sentences.zh: 人们仍有约30%的热量来自面包。

sentences.en: That's so much bread.
sentences.zh: 那真是太多的面包了。

sentences.en: That's bread at every meal, and some meals that were only bread.
sentences.zh: 那是每顿饭都有面包，有些餐食甚至只有面包。

sentences.en: For most of our long history with bread, the bread we ate was made in our homes.
sentences.zh: 在我们与面包漫长的历史中，大部分时间里，我们吃的面包都是在家制作的。

sentences.en: Eventually, we had small bakeries that supplied bread for more people,
sentences.zh: 后来，我们有了为更多人供应面包的小型面包店，

sentences.en: but they weren't exactly a picture of artisanal purity.
sentences.zh: 但它们并不完全是手工纯粹的典范。

sentences.en: A hundred plus years ago, bakeries were generally dirty and often underground,
sentences.zh: 一百多年前，面包店通常很脏，而且往往在地下，

sentences.en: usually with terrible working conditions.
sentences.zh: 工作条件通常很糟糕。

sentences.en: And you never knew when the baker would cut costs by cutting the dough with sawdust or some other horrible additives.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道面包师什么时候会为了削减成本，在面团里掺入锯末或其他可怕的添加剂。

sentences.en: During the time we're talking about, the late 1800s, early 1900s,
sentences.zh: 在我们谈论的那个时期，即19世纪末到20世纪初，

sentences.en: there was a lot of foodborne illness, cholera and typhus.
sentences.zh: 有很多食源性疾病，如霍乱和伤寒。

sentences.en: A lot of Americans were starting to fear their food, and for good reason.
sentences.zh: 许多美国人开始害怕他们的食物，这是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: Your food could kill you.
sentences.zh: 你的食物可能会害死你。

sentences.en: Middle and upper class, white, native-born Americans during that period
sentences.zh: 当时的中上层阶级、白人、本土出生的美国人，

sentences.en: go through this kind of freak out about the safety of their bread.
sentences.zh: 对面包的安全性产生了一种恐慌。

sentences.en: And you see newspaper headlines during this time screaming,
sentences.zh: 你可以看到当时报纸头条惊呼：

sentences.en: Dangerous bread threatens the city.
sentences.zh: 危险的面包威胁城市。

sentences.en: Germs menace your loaf.
sentences.zh: 细菌威胁你的面包。

sentences.en: Things like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: And people were really freaked out.
sentences.zh: 人们真的被吓坏了。

sentences.en: Every city was holding major hearings on the bread question.
sentences.zh: 每个城市都在就面包问题举行重大听证会。

sentences.en: The neighborhood bakery that we romanticize today was this specter of fear and terror.
sentences.zh: 我们今天浪漫化的街区面包店，当时却是恐惧和恐怖的幽灵。

sentences.en: And so people started getting really interested in where their food came from,
sentences.zh: 于是人们开始非常关心食物的来源，

sentences.en: kind of like people are doing right now.
sentences.zh: 就像人们现在所做的那样。

sentences.en: Only to them, knowing where their food came from meant actively avoiding locally baked bread.
sentences.zh: 只不过对他们来说，了解食物来源意味着积极避开本地烘焙的面包。

sentences.en: Factory bread, the thinking went, was born not of unclean hands in an underground furnace,
sentences.zh: 人们认为，工厂面包不是诞生于地下炉膛里不洁的手中，

sentences.en: but in a modern, light-filled palace of industry.
sentences.zh: 而是诞生于现代、明亮、工业化的宫殿中。

sentences.en: These palaces of industry would supply bread to the masses.
sentences.zh: 这些工业宫殿将为大众供应面包。

sentences.en: And this bread would be white.
sentences.zh: 而且这种面包必须是白色的。

sentences.en: Bread is a delicious food.
sentences.zh: 面包是一种美味的食物。

sentences.en: Its flavor blends perfectly with other foods, adding zest and enjoyment to any meal.
sentences.zh: 它的味道能与其他食物完美融合，为任何餐点增添风味和乐趣。

sentences.en: White flour and white bread aren't recent technological innovations in and of themselves.
sentences.zh: 白面粉和白面包本身并不是近期的技术创新。

sentences.en: They've been around for millennia.
sentences.zh: 它们已经存在了几千年。

sentences.en: Technically speaking, white flour is whole wheat flour,
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，白面粉就是全麦面粉，

sentences.en: with the bran and the germ from the wheat kernel sifted out.
sentences.zh: 筛去了小麦仁中的麸皮和胚芽。

sentences.en: Industrial bakers chose white bread as their flagship bread,
sentences.zh: 工业面包师选择白面包作为他们的旗舰产品，

sentences.en: because for them, white was a marker of purity and cleanliness and modernity.
sentences.zh: 因为对他们来说，白色是纯洁、清洁和现代的标志。

sentences.en: And if this sentiment sounds vaguely racist to you?
sentences.zh: 如果这种情绪听起来让你觉得有点种族歧视？

sentences.en: Well, the racism was more than vague.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种种族歧视可不仅仅是“有点”。

sentences.en: Dr. Woods Hutchinson, who was a noted health columnist,
sentences.zh: 伍兹·哈钦森博士，一位著名的健康专栏作家，

sentences.en: syndicated columnist in newspapers,
sentences.zh: 报纸的联合专栏作家，

sentences.en: argued that only white bread would fortify the white race to do the things it had to do
sentences.zh: 他认为只有白面包才能增强白人种族的力量，去完成他们必须做的事情，

sentences.en: and go out and conquer other peoples.
sentences.zh: 去征服其他民族。

sentences.en: And if that's not revolting enough?
sentences.zh: 如果这还不够令人反感的话？

sentences.en: Food reformers of the day referring to the white loaf as a chaste loaf
sentences.zh: 当时的食品改革者将白面包称为“纯洁的面包”，

sentences.en: and the dark loaf as a defiled loaf.
sentences.zh: 而将黑面包称为“玷污的面包”。

sentences.en: And bread was actually never a real vector for a contagion.
sentences.zh: 实际上，面包从来都不是传染病的真正媒介。

sentences.en: That was mostly the meat and dairy supply.
sentences.zh: 那主要是肉类和乳制品供应的问题。

sentences.en: Which is why Aaron Bob Rostrain argues that this fear over the safety of bread
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么亚伦·博布罗·斯特雷恩认为，这种对面包安全性的恐惧，

sentences.en: wasn't actually about bread.
sentences.zh: 实际上与面包无关。

sentences.en: What I started to realize was that it had become
sentences.zh: 我开始意识到，在本土出生的中上层白人的头脑中，

sentences.en: impossible in native-born middle- and upper-class whites minds
sentences.zh: 已经不可能将对面包安全的恐惧，

sentences.en: to separate fears about bread safety from their fears about immigration,
sentences.zh: 与他们对移民的恐惧分离开来，

sentences.en: particularly the new southern and eastern European immigrants
sentences.zh: 特别是那些来自南欧和东欧的新移民，

sentences.en: who supposedly dirty and diseased hands were touching bread in neighborhood bakeries.
sentences.zh: 他们那被认为肮脏且带有病菌的手，正在街区面包店里触摸面包。

sentences.en: Basically, Aaron believes that our attraction to white bread
sentences.zh: 基本上，亚伦认为我们对白面包的偏爱，

sentences.en: came from real fears about food contagion
sentences.zh: 源于对食物传染的真实恐惧，

sentences.en: that got mixed up unfairly with fears about immigrants.
sentences.zh: 这种恐惧被不公平地与对移民的恐惧混为一谈了。

sentences.en: It was a shining, white, clean, modern marvel,
sentences.zh: 它是一个闪亮、洁白、干净的现代奇迹，

sentences.en: untouched by human hands,
sentences.zh: 未被人类之手触碰，

sentences.en: that was the antithesis of that scary, supposedly dirty and diseased product of immigration.
sentences.zh: 它与那种可怕的、被认为肮脏且带有病菌的移民产品形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: And because white bread was white, the thinking went,
sentences.zh: 而且人们认为，因为白面包是白色的，

sentences.en: you knew it was free of dirt and other contaminants,
sentences.zh: 你就知道它没有污垢和其他污染物，

sentences.en: which you might fear from your local bakery.
sentences.zh: 而这些正是你可能从当地面包店里担心的。

sentences.en: Its whiteness was thus its proof of purity.
sentences.zh: 因此，它的洁白就是它纯洁的证明。

sentences.en: Now that logic is kind of flawed because
sentences.zh: 现在这种逻辑有点缺陷，因为

sentences.en: lots of the adulterants that bakers used were white.
sentences.zh: 面包师使用的许多掺假物也是白色的。

sentences.en: Chalk, alum.
sentences.zh: 比如白垩、明矾。

sentences.en: The bleach white loaf just needed one more thing
sentences.zh: 这种漂白过的白面包还需要最后一步，

sentences.en: before it could fully embody our need for uniformity.
sentences.zh: 才能完全体现我们对统一性的需求。

sentences.en: It needed to be sliced.
sentences.zh: 它需要被切片。

sentences.en: Which brings us to a summer day in 1928.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了1928年的一个夏日。

sentences.en: Let's say July 7, 1928.
sentences.zh: 就说是1928年7月7日吧。

sentences.en: On that day, it was July 7th, I checked,
sentences.zh: 那天确实是7月7日，我查过了，

sentences.en: in the town of Chillicothe, Missouri,
sentences.zh: 在密苏里州的奇利科西镇，

sentences.en: people had gathered at First and Elm Streets
sentences.zh: 人们聚集在第一街和榆树街路口，

sentences.en: and they were lined up around the block.
sentences.zh: 他们排队排到了街区转角。

sentences.en: I don't know if there were lines down the block.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是否真的排到了街区外。

sentences.en: Those weren't described.
sentences.zh: 那些并没有被描述过。

sentences.en: But people were certainly eager to see this.
sentences.zh: 但人们肯定很渴望看到这个。

sentences.en: However they were gathered,
sentences.zh: 不管他们是怎么聚集的，

sentences.en: people were there to witness the advent of packaged, pre-sliced bread.
sentences.zh: 人们都在那里见证包装好的预切片面包的问世。

sentences.en: One reporter in Chillicothe, Missouri,
sentences.zh: 密苏里州奇利科西的一位记者，

sentences.en: spoke of housewives who were visiting this bakery
sentences.zh: 谈到了参观这家面包店的家庭主妇们，

sentences.en: to see this sliced bread,
sentences.zh: 她们来看这种切片面包，

sentences.en: how they had this thrill of enthusiasm
sentences.zh: 她们是多么兴奋和热情，

sentences.en: and were just awestruck by this perfectly sliced bread.
sentences.zh: 对这种完美切片的面包感到无比惊叹。

sentences.en: It was a small, edible vision of progress and the future.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于进步和未来的微小、可食用的愿景。

sentences.en: People like sliced bread so much.
sentences.zh: 人们非常喜欢切片面包。

sentences.en: I can't overstate how much they loved it
sentences.zh: 我无法夸大他们有多么喜欢它，

sentences.en: and how quickly it caught on.
sentences.zh: 以及它流行得有多快。

sentences.en: It was the best thing since...
sentences.zh: 这是自……以来最好的发明。

sentences.en: I can't even think of another thing that was quite as good.
sentences.zh: 我甚至想不出还有什么东西能像它一样好。

sentences.en: Industrial bakers had the hype.
sentences.zh: 工业面包师拥有了炒作手段。

sentences.en: They had the sense of moral mission.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有了道德使命感。

sentences.en: And they had the design parameters.
sentences.zh: 他们还拥有了设计参数。

sentences.en: White bread in streamlined loaves with uniform slices.
sentences.zh: 流线型面包，切片均匀的白面包。

sentences.en: But the science of industrializing and mass-producing bread
sentences.zh: 但工业化和大规模生产面包的科学，

sentences.en: was still a little wacky.
sentences.zh: 当时还有点古怪。

sentences.en: Bread, after all,
sentences.zh: 毕竟，面包，

sentences.en: is the product of microorganisms going through biological processes.
sentences.zh: 是微生物进行生物过程的产物。

sentences.en: Bread is a function of time and temperature
sentences.zh: 面包是时间和温度的函数。

sentences.en: and a lot of other variables.
sentences.zh: 以及许多其他变量。

sentences.en: In fact, bread was one of the last major foods to get industrialized
sentences.zh: 事实上，面包是最后几种实现工业化的主要食品之一，

sentences.en: precisely because of how complex it is to make uniformly.
sentences.zh: 恰恰是因为要做到统一生产非常复杂。

sentences.en: The assembly process was really different than, say, making a car.
sentences.zh: 其组装过程与制造汽车之类的东西截然不同。

sentences.en: Imagine if Henry Ford, every time he wanted to make a car,
sentences.zh: 试想一下，如果亨利·福特每次想造一辆车时，

sentences.en: had to worry about the fact that his parts might grow or shrink
sentences.zh: 都得担心他的零件可能会因为当天的温度和湿度

sentences.en: depending on the temperature and humidity that day,
sentences.zh: 而发生膨胀或收缩，

sentences.en: that a gust of air coming through the factory might cause his car to deflate.
sentences.zh: 或者工厂里吹进的一阵风可能会导致他的车瘪掉。

sentences.en: These were the kind of biological questions
sentences.zh: 这些就是早期的工业面包师

sentences.en: that early industrial bakers had to figure out.
sentences.zh: 必须解决的生物学问题。

sentences.en: And so from the 1920s and 30s onward,
sentences.zh: 因此，从20世纪20年代和30年代开始，

sentences.en: industrial bakers were constantly tinkering with the design of white bread.
sentences.zh: 工业面包师们不断地对白面包的设计进行改良。

sentences.en: They cut the time it took for the bread to rise
sentences.zh: 他们通过添加糖分和提高温度，

sentences.en: by adding sugars and cranking up the temperature.
sentences.zh: 缩短了面包发酵所需的时间。

sentences.en: They added emulsifiers to allow the dough's water and fat
sentences.zh: 他们添加了乳化剂，使面团中的水分和油脂

sentences.en: to mix together better,
sentences.zh: 能更好地混合在一起，

sentences.en: giving white bread its height and more even grain.
sentences.zh: 从而使白面包变得更高，组织也更均匀。

sentences.en: That also got rid of the holes.
sentences.zh: 这也消除了面包里的孔洞。

sentences.en: Because wonder soft whipped bread is made from batter, not dough.
sentences.zh: 因为“奇迹”软绵打发面包是用面糊做的，而不是面团。

sentences.en: It has no holes.
sentences.zh: 它没有孔洞。

sentences.en: Get wonder soft whipped.
sentences.zh: 买“奇迹”软绵面包吧。

sentences.en: Eventually, vitamins were added
sentences.zh: 最终，人们添加了维生素，

sentences.en: and sold to the public as a means of making hardy young men
sentences.zh: 并将其作为一种能培养出强壮年轻人的手段向公众销售，

sentences.en: who would be fit to fight in the war.
sentences.zh: 让他们能够胜任战争中的战斗。

sentences.en: Two slices of wonder bread every meal
sentences.zh: 每餐两片“奇迹”面包，

sentences.en: give you as much phosphorus for cell metabolism as this egg,
sentences.zh: 为你提供的细胞代谢磷含量相当于这枚鸡蛋，

sentences.en: as much iron for red blood as three lamb chops,
sentences.zh: 造血所需的铁含量相当于三块羊排，

sentences.en: as much niacin for mental health as six sardines,
sentences.zh: 心理健康所需的烟酸含量相当于六条沙丁鱼，

sentences.en: as much energy as two glasses of milk.
sentences.zh: 提供的能量相当于两杯牛奶。

sentences.en: Little by little,
sentences.zh: 一点一点地，

sentences.en: various factories created their own recipes
sentences.zh: 各个工厂创造出了各自的配方

sentences.en: and innovations for industrial white bread.
sentences.zh: 以及工业白面包的创新技术。

sentences.en: And all of that came to a head in 1952,
sentences.zh: 这一切在1952年达到了顶峰，

sentences.en: in Rockford, Illinois.
sentences.zh: 地点在伊利诺伊州的罗克福德。

sentences.en: The USDA, in cooperation with key figures of the industrial baking world,
sentences.zh: 美国农业部与工业烘焙界的重要人物合作，

sentences.en: put together a multi-year project
sentences.zh: 发起了一个多年项目，

sentences.en: that I kind of jokingly referred to as the Manhattan Project of Bread.
sentences.zh: 我戏称它为“面包界的曼哈顿计划”。

sentences.en: A multi-year panoramic investigation of bread and bread eating habits.
sentences.zh: 这是一项关于面包和吃面包习惯的多年全景式调查。

sentences.en: And the ultimate goal of the project was to design the perfect loaf of white bread.
sentences.zh: 该项目的最终目标是设计出完美的白面包。

sentences.en: It involved focus groups, market research, double-blind taste tests.
sentences.zh: 它涉及焦点小组、市场调研和双盲口味测试。

sentences.en: The end product of the so-called Manhattan Project of Bread
sentences.zh: 所谓的“面包曼哈顿计划”的最终产品，

sentences.en: was a white bread two and a half times as sweet as the average loaf available at the time.
sentences.zh: 是一种甜度是当时市面上普通面包两倍半的白面包。

sentences.en: And 40% fluffier, too.
sentences.zh: 而且还要蓬松40%。

sentences.en: The fluffier the manufacturers made the bread,
sentences.zh: 制造商把面包做得越蓬松，

sentences.en: the more people wanted to buy it,
sentences.zh: 人们就越想买，

sentences.en: even though the Rockford research also showed that they didn't really like it.
sentences.zh: 尽管罗克福德的研究也表明他们其实并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: They just couldn't resist the fluff.
sentences.zh: 他们只是无法抗拒那种蓬松感。

sentences.en: Consumers are choosing the fluffier bread,
sentences.zh: 消费者选择了更蓬松的面包，

sentences.en: but not particularly liking its texture.
sentences.zh: 但并不是特别喜欢它的口感。

sentences.en: But yet they were eating it in large quantities,
sentences.zh: 然而他们却在大量食用，

sentences.en: about a pound and a half per person per week.
sentences.zh: 每人每周大约吃掉一磅半。

sentences.en: Not too long after the Rockford study closes shop,
sentences.zh: 在罗克福德的研究结束后不久，

sentences.en: white bread goes through an identity crisis.
sentences.zh: 白面包经历了一场身份危机。

sentences.en: Where it was once a feel-good symbol of progress,
sentences.zh: 它曾经是进步的象征，让人感觉良好，

sentences.en: white bread began to get used as an epithet,
sentences.zh: 但后来白面包开始被用作一个贬义词，

sentences.en: meaning, you know, stuffy, conservative, square, white suburban.
sentences.zh: 意思是，你知道的，古板、保守、刻板、白人郊区化。

sentences.en: In 1970, when Richard Pryor, in a fit,
sentences.zh: 1970年，当理查德·普赖尔情绪失控，

sentences.en: storms off the stage of his popular show at the Aladdin Theater in Las Vegas,
sentences.zh: 冲下他在拉斯维加斯阿拉丁剧院广受欢迎的演出舞台时，

sentences.en: saying that he is absolutely done with this white bread humor.
sentences.zh: 他说他彻底受够了这种“白面包式”的幽默。

sentences.en: From around that point forward,
sentences.zh: 从那时起，

sentences.en: countercultural movements used white bread as an emblem of the establishment
sentences.zh: 反主流文化运动将白面包用作建制派的象征，

sentences.en: of the silent majority of Richard Nixon's America.
sentences.zh: 象征着理查德·尼克松时代的美国那“沉默的大多数”。

sentences.en: But then...
sentences.zh: 但后来……

sentences.en: By the 1980s, 1990s, the meaning starts to bifurcate.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪80年代、90年代，其含义开始分化。

sentences.en: It also starts to take on the significance of white trash.
sentences.zh: 它也开始带上“白人垃圾”的意味。

sentences.en: So white bread starts to stand in for a poor white person
sentences.zh: 所以白面包开始代表贫穷的白人，

sentences.en: who is making supposedly irresponsible decisions about diet and about their life.
sentences.zh: 他们在饮食和生活上做出了所谓的“不负责任”的决定。

sentences.en: So I was fascinated by the way that white bread could mean essentially the opposite of itself.
sentences.zh: 所以我对白面包竟然能表达出与其自身截然相反的含义感到着迷。

sentences.en: Both affluent and suburban and poor and rural.
sentences.zh: 既代表富裕的郊区，也代表贫穷的乡村。

sentences.en: If there's one lesson from Aaron Bobro Strain's research,
sentences.zh: 如果说亚伦·博布罗·斯特兰的研究能给我们什么启示的话，

sentences.en: it's that this debate over which kind of bread to eat,
sentences.zh: 那就是关于该吃哪种面包的争论，

sentences.en: white or wheat,
sentences.zh: 白面包还是全麦面包，

sentences.en: it's not new.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: In fact, it goes back thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这可以追溯到几千年前。

sentences.en: In Plato's Republic, Plato sets up this kind of debate
sentences.zh: 在柏拉图的《理想国》中，柏拉图提出了这样一种辩论，

sentences.en: about whether the ideal polis, the ideal society or city-state
sentences.zh: 关于理想的城邦，即理想的社会或城市国家，

sentences.en: should function on a diet of whole-grain gruel
sentences.zh: 是否应该以全谷物粥为食，

sentences.en: associated with rural life
sentences.zh: 这与乡村生活相关，

sentences.en: or kind of city-fied white bread cakes.
sentences.zh: 还是应该以城市化的白面包糕点为食。

sentences.en: But what's most interesting about these debates in history, says Aaron,
sentences.zh: 但亚伦说，历史上这些辩论最有趣的地方在于，

sentences.en: is that they are often about everything except bread.
sentences.zh: 它们往往与面包无关。

sentences.en: So in Plato's case...
sentences.zh: 所以在柏拉图的例子中……

sentences.en: Even back then, it was really not about the healthiness of bread
sentences.zh: 即使在当时，这其实也不是关于面包的健康与否，

sentences.en: so much as it was about anxieties about whether
sentences.zh: 更多的是关于人们的焦虑，担心

sentences.en: the Athens was losing moral virtue
sentences.zh: 雅典是否正在失去道德美德，

sentences.en: because it was becoming less connected to the land.
sentences.zh: 因为它与土地的联系越来越少了。

sentences.en: We see that debates about white bread and brown bread
sentences.zh: 我们看到，关于白面包和黑面包的争论，

sentences.en: get tied up into large questions about
sentences.zh: 被卷入了关于以下重大问题的讨论中：

sentences.en: what do people think about progress?
sentences.zh: 人们如何看待进步？

sentences.en: What do people think about industrialization,
sentences.zh: 人们如何看待工业化、

sentences.en: class, and hierarchy?
sentences.zh: 阶级和等级制度？

sentences.en: The point is, is that when we're worrying about whether or not
sentences.zh: 重点是，当我们担心是否

sentences.en: we should eat white bread or brown bread,
sentences.zh: 应该吃白面包还是黑面包时，

sentences.en: it's usually about much larger questions.
sentences.zh: 这通常关乎更大的问题。

sentences.en: We can learn something about our own society,
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过审视那些关于什么才算好面包的争论，

sentences.en: our own anxieties and aspirations
sentences.zh: 了解我们自己的社会，

sentences.en: by looking at those debates about what counts as good bread.
sentences.zh: 了解我们自己的焦虑和抱负。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由萨姆·格林斯潘制作。

sentences.en: And here's Sammy really going to town on Wonder Bread.
sentences.zh: 萨米在这里真的对“奇迹”面包大加赞赏。

sentences.en: With Katie Mingle, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 还有凯蒂·明格尔、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: It is based on an interview we heard on Benjamin Walker's Theory of Everything,
sentences.zh: 它基于我们在本杰明·沃克的《万物理论》中听到的一次采访，

sentences.en: a fine Radiotopia program that you should already love.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很棒的Radiotopia节目，你应该早就喜欢它了。

sentences.en: On Benjamin's most recent episode,
sentences.zh: 在本杰明最近的一期节目中，

sentences.en: we tell the story of how Benjamin and I first met 14 years ago
sentences.zh: 我们讲述了本杰明和我14年前第一次见面，

sentences.en: and started immediately conspiring to make something like we've made in Radiotopia today,
sentences.zh: 并立即开始密谋制作像今天在Radiotopia上看到的那样的节目，

sentences.en: a place where the most creative radio makers
sentences.zh: 一个让最有创意的广播制作人

sentences.en: produce directly for the most curious and engaged listeners.
sentences.zh: 直接为最好奇、最投入的听众制作节目的地方。

sentences.en: You should check it out.
sentences.zh: 你应该去听听看。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7, local public radio, KALW, in San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山当地公共广播电台KALW 91.7的一个项目，

sentences.en: and produced out of the offices of ArcSign,
sentences.zh: 制作于ArcSign的办公室，

sentences.en: an architecture firm in beautiful downtown Raycat country, Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 那是一家位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽地区的建筑事务所。

sentences.en: You can follow along with this show on Facebook, Twitter, and Tumblr,
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook、Twitter和Tumblr上关注这个节目，

sentences.en: and everything you ever need to know about this show,
sentences.zh: 关于这个节目你需要知道的一切，

sentences.en: you can find out on 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 都可以在99pi.org上找到。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
